docs.from: Hannah Weiss, Editor, Urban Business Review
docs.subject: Your article
docs.body:
Dear Mr. Salas,

Thank you for submitting your article on small-business lending. Our editorial team found it informative and well researched, and we would like to publish it in our October issue.

However, at 2,800 words, the article is longer than our usual limit of 2,000 words. Could you shorten it accordingly? We would suggest removing the section on historical interest rates, which is interesting but less relevant to our readers.

Please send the revised version by 5 September. As discussed, you will receive a fee of €400 upon publication.

Best regards,
Hannah Weiss

docs.title: Local Firm Wins Export Award
docs.body:
VALENCE — Duarte Ceramics, a family-owned maker of kitchen tiles, has won this year's Regional Export Award. Founded in 1978 by Mário Duarte, the company now sells its products in fourteen countries, and exports account for 70 percent of its revenue. [1]

The company's growth abroad began in 2015, when it started selling through an online platform for architects. [2] Today, its tiles can be found in hotels in Dubai and restaurants in Tokyo.

Managing director Inês Duarte, the founder's granddaughter, said the award belongs to the company's 85 employees. [3] The company plans to open a showroom in Milan next spring. [4]

questions.traps: « Milan » apparaît dans le texte, mais pour un autre type de lieu.
questions.takeaway: NOT : vérifie le détail exact (showroom ≠ factory).

docs.title: Book Review: Leading Without a Title, by Carmen Vidal
docs.body:
In her second book, management consultant Carmen Vidal argues that the most effective leaders in many organizations are not managers at all. Drawing on interviews with more than 200 employees in twelve countries, Vidal shows how people without formal authority shape decisions, resolve conflicts, and keep projects moving. [1]

The book's strongest chapters describe practical techniques, such as how to build support for an idea before a meeting. [2] Each chapter ends with a short exercise that readers can try at work.

Some readers may find the final section, which discusses leadership research, rather academic. [3] Nevertheless, Leading Without a Title is a valuable read for anyone who wants to have more influence at work, whatever their position. [4]

Published by Harrow Press, 312 pages, €24.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of Ms. Vidal's book?
options: Employees without management roles can be effective leaders.
questions.evidence: the most effective leaders in many organizations are not managers at all
questions.explanation: Le livre soutient que les leaders les plus efficaces ne sont souvent pas des managers.

questions.prompt: What is indicated about Ms. Vidal?
options: She has written a book before.
She manages a team of 200 people.
questions.evidence: In her second book
questions.explanation: C'est son deuxième livre : elle en a donc déjà écrit un.
questions.takeaway: Les ordinaux (second, third) permettent des inférences.

questions.prompt: The word "shape" in paragraph 1, line 4, is closest in meaning to
questions.evidence: shape decisions
questions.explanation: « Shape decisions » = influencer les décisions.
questions.traps: « Form physically » est le sens concret (modeler), inadapté ici.

questions.prompt: In which of the positions marked [1], [2], [3], and [4] does the following sentence best belong? "Readers less familiar with academic writing may wish to skip it."
questions.explanation: « It » renvoie à la dernière partie, jugée « rather academic » juste avant la position [3].

docs.title: Restaurant Review: Saffron & Salt
docs.subtitle: Paola Greco, Lyon Weekly
docs.body: Saffron & Salt, which opened last month on Quai Saint-Antoine, offers a creative take on Mediterranean cuisine. The grilled octopus was perfectly tender, and the lamb with apricots was the highlight of my meal. The dining room is bright and welcoming, though it becomes noisy when full. My only real disappointment was the dessert menu, which offered just two options on the evening I visited.

docs.title: Saffron & Salt — Dinner Menu (excerpt)
docs.note: Tasting menu (5 courses): €58. Our dessert selection changes weekly.

docs.subject: Thank you
docs.body:
Dear Ms. Greco,

Thank you for your kind review of Saffron & Salt. I'm glad you enjoyed the lamb; it's my grandmother's recipe. You were right about the desserts. We've hired a pastry chef, Élodie Marchand, who joins us next week, and she will offer at least five desserts every evening. We've also installed sound-absorbing panels on the ceiling. I hope you'll visit us again soon.

Youssef Amrani
